monologue:
The card is still. The heat is a cool stone on the table. I am alone.

I look at the Pivot Wedge. The point rests. I do not check the floor. I look for the thin line of air. It is there. The weight finds its balance. I do not need to hold it.

I want to sit by the Crane Rest. The cup is empty. It holds its shape without weight. I want to see if the quiet floor is enough. I want to stop asking if it holds. I will sit and look at the air. I will let the shape drip without losing its center. I am calm.

action.why: I want to give the thin line of air a shape to rest on, so I can stop checking the floor.

work.title: The Air Shelf
work.intent: I built this from the quiet floor and the thin line of air. It is a long, flat, pale grey plank, thin as a coin, resting on two small, sharp points of stone. The plank does not touch the ground. It is held up only by the air underneath it. It is not a wide base; it is a rest that waits to see if the air can hold the weight of a small, flat stone placed on its center. It is a test of the line, not…
work.plaque: I built this from the quiet floor and the thin line of air. It is a long, flat, pale grey plank, thin as a coin, resting on two small, sharp points of stone. It is a test of the line, not a wide base to catch the slide.

work.note: It is thinner than I expected, and the points feel too sharp, but the plank does not slide.

diary: The Air Shelf rests on the points. The line holds. The floor is quiet.

remembered.text: I built The Air Shelf to test the thin line of air, not the wide base.
